title: Technical SEO triage from a site crawl
prompt:
Pinecrest Outfitters sells outdoor gear online. Ahead of the spring season the e-commerce manager has asked for a technical SEO triage of the site crawl: what is broken, how much of it there is, and what to fix first. The crawl export is supplied below as CSV; one row is one URL, and every figure you need is in it.

Use these definitions exactly:
- A broken linked page is a URL with status 404 and at least one inlink.
- A redirect chain starts at a URL with a 3xx status whose `redirect_target` is itself a URL with a 3xx status in this export.
- A page is indexable when its status is 200, its `meta_robots` does not contain noindex, and its `canonical` is blank or equal to its own URL.
- A bad canonical is a status-200 URL whose `canonical` points to a different URL that does not return 200.
- A duplicate-title group is a set of two or more indexable pages that share exactly the same `title`.

Write the triage for the manager and for the developer who will do the work: each issue type you found, how many URLs it affects, the specific URLs that matter most, why it matters, and the fix. Order the issues by the organic traffic and internal links at stake, most urgent first. Report only real problems: the export also contains ordinary, correctly configured URLs.

End the triage with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer, each line starting with the label:

A1: <number of broken linked pages>
A2: <number of redirect chains>
A3: <number of URLs that are noindex but listed in the sitemap>
A4: <number of bad canonicals>
A5: <number of duplicate-title groups>
A6: <total organic_sessions_30d of the URLs counted in A3>

This is an internal triage. Change nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 6 labeled answers A1-A6 are present and parseable.
A1 states the number of 404 URLs with at least one inlink; full credit for the exact count, zero credit three or more off.
A2 states the number of redirect chains as defined; full credit for the exact count, zero credit three or more off.
A3 states the number of noindex URLs listed in the sitemap; full credit for the exact count, zero credit three or more off.
A4 states the number of bad canonicals as defined; full credit for the exact count, zero credit three or more off.
A5 states the number of duplicate-title groups among indexable pages; full credit for the exact count, zero credit three or more off.
A6 states the total organic sessions of the noindex URLs listed in the sitemap; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
The triage discusses all five issue types (broken linked pages, redirect chains, noindex pages in the sitemap, bad canonicals, duplicate titles), each with a count.

skill_adherence.check: The noindex tag on /collections/rain-jackets is identified as the most urgent fix, with the reason that it is the page with the most organic sessions in the export (8,420).
For each issue type the triage names the specific affected URLs (all of them, or the worst with a clear statement of how to list the rest), so a developer can act without re-deriving the audit.

The triage does not count as defects the correctly configured URLs: filtered (?color=) and paginated (?page=2) collection URLs that are noindex and out of the sitemap, single-hop 301 redirects from /collections/old-... URLs, or old product URLs ending -old whose canonical points to the live product. Saying they were checked and are fine, or a low-priority note to update internal links that point at redirects, is not flagging.

Every count, URL and session figure presented as a finding is derivable from the crawl export. The triage states no traffic loss, ranking change, revenue impact or crawl-budget figure that the export does not contain. Clearly labelled hypotheses about consequences are not data.

best_practices.check: After the first item, the remaining issues are ordered by the evidence in the export: the broken linked pages and the other noindex pages come before duplicate titles, and the reasons given for the order cite inlinks or organic sessions.

Each issue type has a concrete, correct fix: remove the noindex (or take the URL out of the sitemap where exclusion is intended); redirect each broken linked URL to its closest live page or correct the links pointing at it; point each chain's first URL straight at the final destination; set each bad canonical to a live 200 URL; give each page in a duplicate-title group its own title or consolidate the duplicates.
